I do think that what’s happened with Voyager 1 and also Voyager 2 is amazing and beautiful, and they’re phenomenal achievements of humanity that will go down in history. At the same time, nothing lasts forever, and Voyager 1, and I think also Voyager 2, are both slated to essentially go dark no later than about 2036, about 10 years from now. And that’s because their radioactive, nuclear power sources that give them heat and electricity way out there, where things like solar power won’t work ’cause they’re so far away, uh, will diminish to essentially nothing due to radioactive decay. They will no longer be able to send signals back. They’ll no longer be able to stay warm, and so they’ll freeze and go dark. Obviously that’s at most 10 years away. I think perhaps it’s optimistic to think that they will reach that point because they’re already hanging on by a thread.
paras.zh: 比林斯：所以我不想成为一个沮丧的人。我确实认为航海家一号和航海家二号所发生的事情是令人惊叹和美丽的，它们是人类的非凡成就，将载入史册。与此同时，没有什么是永恒的，航海者 1 号和我认为航海者 2 号都预计将在 2036 年左右（即从现在起大约 10 年后）基本上陷入黑暗。那是因为它们的放射性核动力源为它们提供热量和电力，而太阳能之类的东西则无法工作，因为它们距离太远，呃，由于放射性衰变，它们将基本上消失殆尽。他们将无法再发回信号。它们将不再能够保持温暖，因此它们会被冻住并变黑。显然，这最多还需要10年的时间。我认为也许乐观地认为他们会达到这一点，因为他们已经命悬一线了。

paras.en: Some people at NASA were very concerned that Voyager 1 wouldn’t even be awake, so to speak, to see this light-day milestone because they have been having a lot of trouble with keeping its instruments on. They have been shutting down instruments and components on these spacecraft to continue to use them on the small trickle of electricity, of power that still comes from these radioactive power sources. And so we do have some, some time still left in their life, so enjoy them while you can.
paras.zh: NASA 的一些人非常担心航海者 1 号甚至不会醒来，可以说，看到这个光日里程碑，因为他们在保持仪器开启方面遇到了很多麻烦。他们一直在关闭这些航天器上的仪器和组件，以继续使用仍然来自这些放射性电源的少量电力。因此，他们的生命中确实还剩下一些时间，所以趁你还可以的时候享受它们吧。

paras.en: Feltman: Always good advice. Well, let’s move on to another piece of space news that people may have seen recently, that has to do with reusable rockets and some chopsticks, some big ol’ space chopsticks.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：总是好的建议。好吧，让我们转向人们最近可能看到的另一条太空新闻，这与可重复使用的火箭和一些筷子有关，一些大的太空筷子。

paras.en: Billings: Oh, goodness, goodness, goodness. Yes, yes, of course. Well, I hope everyone’s heard about this because it is a very big deal. SpaceX’s experimental Starship, a fully reusable megarocket that’s just giant, it’s hard to envision the scale of this thing, went up into orbit, it deployed some Starlink satellites, and then it came back to Earth, and it flew back to its launch site, and it precision flew and slid in kinda like a glove into its launch tower, which then deployed these, yes, these mechanical arms that are called chopsticks and plucked it out of midair. I guess you could say that if they’re chopsticks, then the Starship upper stage that did this is like the world’s biggest egg roll, and it plucked it right out of midair.
paras.zh: 比林斯：哦，天哪，天哪，天哪。是的，是的，当然。好吧，我希望每个人都听说过这件事，因为这是一件大事。 SpaceX 的实验星舰，一个完全可重复使用的巨型火箭，非常巨大，很难想象它的规模，进入轨道，部署了一些星链卫星，然后返回地球，飞回发射场，它精确地飞行并像手套一样滑入发射塔，然后部署这些，是的，这些被称为筷子的机械臂，并将其从半空中拔出。我想你可能会说，如果它们是筷子，那么星舰上层做这件事就像世界上最大的鸡蛋卷一样，它直接从半空中把它夹了起来。

paras.en: And the reason why this is a big deal is because that’s never, ever, ever been done before. This is something out of science fiction. The engineering behind this is staggering. Only SpaceX has managed to do it, and it matters because if they can catch these things routinely and then fly them again very quickly—that’s the whole point of catching them like this—then you are in a new era of spaceflight. You are in a place where, all of a sudden, instead of launching this thing, you know, maybe at best once every few days or once a week or once a month, you might be launching it a dozen times a day. And that is a very wild prospect, and I don’t think anyone’s really ready for what the world literally looks like if that happens. I can’t emphasize enough how much of a change and a shift that would be in what we can put into space, and also, frankly, some of the environmental effects we might have to deal with from such a rapid uptick in launches. So it is a very, very big deal, and people looking back 100 years from now will probably look at that moment, and they’ll forget about the light-day, and they’ll say, “Oh, that was when, uh, SpaceX managed to catch the upper stage of Starship with the chopsticks.”
paras.zh: 这之所以是一件大事，是因为以前从未这样做过。这是科幻小说中的东西。这背后的工程技术令人震惊。只有 SpaceX 成功做到了这一点，这很重要，因为如果他们能够定期捕捉这些东西，然后很快地再次飞行它们——这就是像这样捕捉它们的全部意义——那么你就进入了航天的新时代。你知道，你突然之间就不再启动这个东西了，最好是每隔几天、每周一次或每月一次，而可能是每天启动十几次。这是一个非常疯狂的前景，我认为没有人真正准备好迎接这种情况发生时世界的实际情况。我无法充分强调我们可以投入太空的东西将会有多大的变化和转变，而且坦率地说，我们可能必须应对发射数量如此迅速增加所带来的一些环境影响。所以这是一件非常非常大的事情，100 年后的人们回顾过去，可能会看到那一刻，他们会忘记光日，他们会说，“哦，那时候，嗯，SpaceX 成功地用筷子抓住了星舰的上层。”

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Before we move on, one last question on that. Could you tell us briefly what it is about catching the rocket in air that makes it so much more practically, you know, reusable than having it land back on the ground?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。在我们继续之前，还有最后一个问题。您能否简单地告诉我们，在空中捕获火箭的原因是什么，使得它比让它降落在地面上更加实用，可以重复使用？

paras.en: Billings: So I think a lot of it has to do with, in some sense, with the tower rather than the rocket. Because people think about these rockets going off into space and shooting into orbit, and they focus on the rocket, and they don’t really pay a lot of attention to the launchpad or the launch tower. But those are critical pieces of infrastructure in this equation as well. And we’ve seen in the past what happens when a rocket as mighty as Starship interacts with its big plume of exhaust, its fiery plume of gas coming out of its rocket engines. What happens when that stuff hits that, sort of, infrastructure? A direct hit can be pretty nasty. And you can reinforce that infrastructure, but it’s probably easier just to minimize the sandblasting effects and the flambéing that happens with a more direct exposure. So you catch it in midair, you ideally preserve more of the readiness of the tower itself and also, frankly, the rocket. The rocket is gonna have to go through a significant, kind of, g-force experience when it shudders to a stop on the ground. And if you can minimize that stuff you notionally can launch much faster and do a faster turnaround.
paras.zh: 比林斯：所以我认为，从某种意义上说，这很大程度上与塔有关，而不是与火箭有关。因为人们想到这些火箭进入太空并射入轨道，他们关注的是火箭，而没有真正关注发射台或发射塔。但这些也是这个等式中基础设施的关键部分。我们过去已经看到过，当像星舰这样强大的火箭与它的大尾气相互作用时会发生什么，从火箭发动机中喷出的炽热气体羽流。当这些东西撞击到基础设施时会发生什么？直接打击可能会非常糟糕。您可以加固该基础设施，但尽量减少喷砂效果和更直接暴露时发生的燃烧可能更容易。所以你在半空中抓住它，理想情况下你可以保留塔本身以及火箭的更多准备状态。当火箭在地面上停下来时，它必须经历一次重要的、某种重力体验。如果你能最大限度地减少这些东西，理论上你可以更快地启动并完成更快的周转。

paras.en: Feltman: Yeah. Well, okay, there’s one more big space story we’re gonna discuss today. It’s a mission that—I was wondering, why does this sound like the name of a restaurant in Midtown or perhaps an uncle of mine?—and it’s because it’s named after a man named Giuseppe. So tell us about BepiColombo. That’s why that name sounds like that.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：是的。好吧，今天我们要讨论一个更大的太空故事。这是一项使命——我想知道，为什么这听起来像中城一家餐馆的名字，或者可能是我叔叔的名字？——因为它是以一个名叫朱塞佩的人的名字命名的。请告诉我们有关 BepiColombo 的信息。这就是为什么这个名字听起来像这样。

paras.en: Billings: BepiColombo, yes. It honestly is my favorite space mission name to say. Can I just, just give me a minute here? BepiColombo. BepiColombo. BepiColombo. I love saying it. It’s so good.
paras.zh: 比林斯：贝皮科伦坡，是的。老实说，这是我最喜欢的太空任务名称。我可以在这里等一下吗？贝皮科伦坡。贝皮科伦坡。贝皮科伦坡。我喜欢这么说。太好了。

paras.en: As you said, it’s named in honor of a man named Giuseppe. Actually, Giuseppe, nickname “Bepi,” Colombo. And he died in 1984. He was an Italian mathematician and engineer, and he is most well known for being the first person to really figure out that you could use what’s called a gravity assist flyby to get to Mercury.
paras.zh: 正如你所说，它的名字是为了纪念一个名叫朱塞佩的人。事实上，朱塞佩，绰号“贝皮”，科伦坡。他于 1984 年去世。他是一位意大利数学家和工程师，他最为人所知的是，他是第一个真正发现可以利用重力辅助飞越水星的人。

paras.en: And NASA actually did that with the Mariner 10 spacecraft. The point is, though, is that he’s somewhat of a legend in the study of Mercury, and so this spacecraft is named in honor of him. And it’s extremely fitting because it turns out BepiColombo had kind of a wild ride to Mercury that took a little, you know, took a lot of these gravitational assists and, I think, even more than originally were planned.
paras.zh: 美国宇航局实际上用水手 10 号宇宙飞船做到了这一点。但关键是，他在水星研究方面是一位传奇人物，因此这艘航天器以他的名字命名。这非常合适，因为事实证明，贝皮科伦坡到水星的旅程有点疯狂，需要一点，你知道，需要很多重力的帮助，我认为，甚至比最初计划的还要多。

paras.en: Feltman: So tell us when it launched and what the big milestone is that we’re talking about now.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：请告诉我们它是什么时候推出的，以及我们现在正在讨论的重大里程碑是什么。

paras.en: Billings: So it launched, actually, back in October 2018, and it was originally supposed to get to Mercury, if I remember correctly, last year, like last December. But what happened was that, in 2024, some electric thrusters on the spacecraft lost power, and so what needed to happen after that was spacecraft engineers, mission planners needed to find a new trajectory to Mercury and rejigger the mission while it’s in motion, while it’s in space, to find a different way to get to Mercury. And that required a lower-thrust trajectory, and in the end, what we saw was BepiColombo—God, I love saying the name—BepiColombo doing one flyby of Earth, two flybys of Venus and six flybys of Mercury.
paras.zh: 比林斯：实际上，它早在 2018 年 10 月就发射了，如果我没记错的话，它最初应该到达水星，是在去年，比如去年 12 月。但发生的事情是，在 2024 年，航天器上的一些电动推进器失去了动力，所以在那之后需要发生的是航天器工程师、任务规划者需要找到一条通往水星的新轨道，并在它在太空中运动时重新调整任务，找到一种不同的方式来到达水星。这需要较低推力的轨道，最后，我们看到的是 BepiColombo——上帝，我喜欢说这个名字——BepiColombo 完成了一次飞越地球、两次飞越金星和六次飞越水星。

paras.en: And you think to yourself, “Wait, six flybys of Mercury? Come on, it’s going to Mercury. You’re telling me it’s already been to Mercury?” Well it gets complicated because it turns out that we started this conversation talking about Voyager 1, the most distant object that we’ve ever sent out there. In some ways, it’s actually harder to get closer into the sun for a spacecraft, and what is the closest planet to the sun, Rachel?
paras.zh: 你心里想，“等等，六次飞越水星？得了吧，它要去水星。你是说它已经飞过水星了？”好吧，事情变得很复杂，因为事实证明我们开始这次谈话是在谈论航行者一号，这是我们发射过的最遥远的物体。从某些方面来说，对于航天器来说，接近太阳实际上更困难，距离太阳最近的行星是哪一颗，雷切尔？

paras.en: Billings: Mercury. So that is one of the hardest places to get to in the solar system. The reason why is because you actually have to bleed off a lot of speed to get down there. And so the normal way you’d do that is by firing your engines to bleed off that speed, but if your engines are malfunctioning and not giving you as much thrust as you need, you’ve gotta bleed it off in a different way. That’s where all these extra flybys came in, and the reason why it’s bleeding off that speed is because it doesn’t want to just fly by. It wants to go into orbit. We’re trying to orbit Mercury.
paras.zh: 比林斯：水星。所以这是太阳系中最难到达的地方之一。原因是因为你实际上必须付出很大的速度才能到达那里。因此，通常的做法是点燃发动机以降低该速度，但如果发动机出现故障并且无法提供所需的推力，则必须以不同的方式降低速度。这就是所有这些额外的飞越进来的地方，而它降低速度的原因是因为它不想只是飞过。它想进入轨道。我们正在尝试绕水星运行。

paras.en: Feltman: Right. Not just whiz right past.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：对。不只是一闪而过。

paras.en: Feltman: So we’re recording this on the 19th [of November], but, by the time this airs, hopefully something very exciting will have happened. Could you tell us more?
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：所以我们将在[11 月] 19 日录制这个节目，但是，当节目播出时，希望会发生一些非常令人兴奋的事情。您能告诉我们更多吗？

paras.en: Billings: Of course. Yes, yes. So I believe on November 21st, BepiColombo is going to go for orbit insertion. This is the point when it actually will officially be captured into Mercury’s orbit, and it’s an elaborate sequence. There’s like 16 or more different maneuvers. Some folks on the mission have called it six months of continuous activities.
paras.zh: 比林斯：当然。是的，是的。所以我相信BepiColombo将在11月21日进入轨道。这是它实际上将被正式捕获到水星轨道的时刻，这是一个精心设计的序列。大约有 16 种或更多不同的动作。一些参与该任务的人称其为六个月的连续活动。

paras.en: It also has multiple different components to deploy. In some respects, BepiColombo, kind of like the name, you know, there’s the Bepi and there’s the Colombo part, is two spacecraft in one. There is something from the European Space Agency called the Mercury Planetary Orbiter that’s gonna be studying the planet’s surface and its interior.
paras.zh: 它还需要部署多个不同的组件。在某些方面，BepiColombo，有点像它的名字，你知道，有 Bepi 部分，还有 Colombo 部分，是两艘航天器合二为一。欧洲航天局有一个叫做水星行星轨道器的东西，它将研究水星的表面和内部。

paras.en: And then the Japanese space agency [the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency], I like to just call it JAXA for short, has contributed a second spacecraft, a second orbiter called Mio, which is going to be looking at Mercury’s magnetosphere, basically, how the solar wind and space weather interacts with the natural geodynamo, the big, planetary-scale magnetic field that exists around Mercury.
paras.zh: 然后，日本航天局（日本宇宙航空研究开发机构），我喜欢简称为 JAXA，贡献了第二艘航天器，第二艘名为 Mio 的轨道飞行器，它将观察水星的磁层，基本上是太阳风和太空天气如何与自然地球发电机（水星周围存在的大型行星尺度磁场）相互作用。

paras.en: And deploying all those in sequence, making sure that they all separate and go into their separate orbits takes some time. And so, you know, even though a lot of excitement is due with the initial capture into orbit, the real fireworks are hopefully going to start next year. We’re looking actually at, like, I think it’s April, early April of 2027 for routine science to begin for these two spacecraft around Mercury.
paras.zh: 按顺序部署所有这些，确保它们全部分离并进入各自的轨道需要一些时间。所以，你知道，尽管最初进入轨道会让人兴奋不已，但真正的烟火有望在明年开始。我们实际上正在考虑，比如，我认为 2027 年 4 月，4 月初，这两个围绕水星的航天器将开始进行常规科学研究。

paras.en: Feltman: Very cool. Well, we’ll definitely have you back to talk about some of those questions and hopefully answers as the science comes in. But thank you so much for sharing some space news with us today.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：非常酷。好吧，我们肯定会让您回来讨论其中一些问题，并希望随着科学的到来得到答案。但非常感谢您今天与我们分享一些太空新闻。

paras.en: Billings: It’s my pleasure, as always, to talk about space news. And once more with feeling: BepiColombo.
paras.zh: 比林斯：一如既往，我很高兴谈论太空新闻。再次充满感情：BepiColombo。

paras.en: That’s all for this week’s news roundup. We’ll be back on Wednesday to talk about an insightful new biography of Stephen Hawking.
paras.zh: 这就是本周新闻综述的全部内容。我们将于周三回来讨论一本富有洞察力的史蒂芬·霍金新传记。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great week!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。祝你度过愉快的一周！

articles.title: What’s really driving the Ebola outbreak?

paras.en: For Marie-Roseline Bélizaire, a typical day starts around 6 A.M. at a health center in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, where she pores over freshly confirmed Ebola cases that have come in overnight. From then on, the work is nonstop: she calls dozens of provinces, visits health centers, supervises contact tracing, trains emergency workers and woos donors—as well as any number of other urgent tasks—before she falls asleep and does it all again the next day.
paras.zh: 对于 Marie-Roseline Bélizaire 来说，典型的一天从早上 6 点左右开始。在刚果民主共和国的一个医疗中心，她在那里仔细研究隔夜出现的新确诊的埃博拉病例。从那时起，工作就不间断了：她给数十个省份打电话，走访卫生中心，监督接触者追踪，培训急救人员，争取捐助者，以及许多其他紧急任务，然后在她入睡之前，第二天再做这一切。

paras.en: Bélizaire, emergency director for the World Health Organization’s Regional Office for Africa, does not expect this work to let up anytime soon. She is on the front line, trying desperately to contain the current Ebola outbreak as it rages across central Africa.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织非洲区域办事处应急主任贝利扎尔预计这项工作不会很快停止。她奋战在前线，拼命遏制正在非洲中部肆虐的埃博拉疫情。

paras.en: “Our biggest concern right now is that the outbreak is still evolving, and we’re still having a lot of people dying in the community,” she says.
paras.zh: “我们现在最担心的是疫情仍在发展，社区中仍有很多人死亡，”她说。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: This Ebola outbreak was declared in the DRC in May. By November 17, it had expanded to five countries, with more than 11,600 recorded cases and more than 5,600 deaths. The disease is being driven by a distinct species of virus called Bundibugyo. After a 2014–2016 outbreak of a different Ebola-causing virus in West Africa (in which Guinea, Liberia and Sierra Leone were the hardest-hit countries), this is the second-largest outbreak of the disease in history and the fastest-spreading ever.
paras.zh: 刚果民主共和国五月份宣布爆发埃博拉疫情。截至 11 月 17 日，疫情已扩展到 5 个国家，记录病例超过 11,600 例，死亡人数超过 5,600 人。这种疾病是由一种名为 Bundibugyo 的独特病毒引起的。继 2014 年至 2016 年西非（其中几内亚、利比里亚和塞拉利昂是受灾最严重的国家）爆发另一种埃博拉病毒后，这是该疾病历史上第二大规模的爆发，也是有史以来传播速度最快的一次。

paras.en: Scientists know little about Bundibugyo and how to treat it clinically—but the public health crisis will take far more than medical measures to solve, experts say.
paras.zh: 专家表示，科学家们对本迪布焦以及如何进行临床治疗知之甚少，但解决这场公共卫生危机需要的不仅仅是医疗措施。

paras.en: Bundibugyo is a rare species of Ebola-causing virus. It has seen only two previous outbreaks, in 2007 and 2012. Symptoms of Bundibugyo infection, as with other cases of Ebola, include fever, diarrhea, vomiting, headaches and difficulty breathing. Because experts have seen so little of this species of virus before and because the DRC is in social and political turmoil, it’s difficult to determine the exact death rate or how the strain might be evolving.
paras.zh: 本迪布焦是一种罕见的埃博拉病毒。此前仅在 2007 年和 2012 年爆发过两次疫情。与其他埃博拉病例一样，本迪布焦感染的症状包括发烧、腹泻、呕吐、头痛和呼吸困难。由于专家们之前很少见到这种病毒，而且刚果民主共和国正处于社会和政治动荡之中，因此很难确定确切的死亡率或病毒株可能如何进化。

paras.en: When virologists were developing vaccines for Ebola during the 2014–2016 outbreak, they did not include Bundibugyo. In primate studies, Bundibugyo appeared less lethal and did not act as fast as other strains, says Tom Geisbert, a virologist at the University of Texas Medical Branch at Galveston. Geisbert helped develop the Ervebo vaccine, which treats the Ebola virus (formerly the Zaire virus), a different species than Bundibugyo. Now, Geisbert says, Bundibugyo’s slow-to-appear symptoms mean that asymptomatic people may infect others for days before they are diagnosed themselves.
paras.zh: 2014-2016 年埃博拉疫情爆发期间，病毒学家在开发埃博拉疫苗时，并未将本迪布焦纳入其中。加尔维斯顿德克萨斯大学医学分部的病毒学家汤姆·盖斯伯特 (Tom Geisbert) 表示，在灵长类动物研究中，本迪布焦似乎不像其他毒株那样致命，而且起效速度也慢。盖斯伯特帮助开发了 Ervebo 疫苗，该疫苗可治疗埃博拉病毒（以前的扎伊尔病毒），该病毒与本迪布焦是不同的物种。盖斯伯特说，现在，本迪布焦的症状出现得很慢，这意味着无症状的人可能会在自己被诊断出来之前的几天内感染他人。

paras.en: “We guessed wrong,” he says of the past vaccine effort. “There just wasn’t enough effort put on Bundibugyo to be ready for that.”
paras.zh: “我们猜错了，”他谈到过去的疫苗工作时说道。 “本迪布焦没有做出足够的努力来为此做好准备。”

paras.en: Research is now underway on potential Bundibugyo vaccines, including Ervebo, along with a vaccine from the University of Oxford that specifically targets Bundibugyo and an mRNA-based vaccine from Moderna. All three have been approved for a phase 2/3 trial that will test the shots on participants in the outbreak zone. Geisbert says he hopes to see a vaccine approved in the first quarter of 2027.
paras.zh: 目前正在研究潜在的 Bundibugyo 疫苗，包括 Ervebo、牛津大学专门针对 Bundibugyo 的疫苗以及来自 Moderna 的基于 mRNA 的疫苗。这三者均已获准进行 2/3 阶段试验，该试验将对疫情爆发区的参与者进行注射测试。盖斯伯特表示，他希望看到疫苗在 2027 年第一季度获得批准。

paras.en: But many of the reasons for the outbreak’s rapid growth aren’t clinical—and the crisis will not end with the arrival of a vaccine.
paras.zh: 但疫情快速增长的许多原因都不是临床原因，而且危机不会随着疫苗的出现而结束。

paras.en: Successful treatment for infectious disease relies on contact tracing: accurate tracking of whom a patient could have infected. Right now, about 65 percent of Ebola deaths are happening within community settings, rather than at well-equipped treatment centers. That makes it more difficult to track infected or exposed people’s movements. The DRC’s health ministry recently said that its tracing rate for known contacts had reached roughly 86 percent, but John Johnson, a vaccination and epidemic response adviser at Doctors Without Borders, says he’d be “shocked” if any of the 68 affected health zones in the country were able to track such a high proportion of the actual number of people exposed.
paras.zh: 传染病的成功治疗依赖于接触者追踪：准确追踪患者可能感染的人。目前，约 65% 的埃博拉死亡病例发生在社区环境中，而不是在设备齐全的治疗中心。这使得追踪感染者或暴露者的活动变得更加困难。刚果民主共和国卫生部最近表示，其对已知接触者的追踪率已达到约 86%，但无国界医生组织的疫苗接种和流行病应对顾问约翰·约翰逊表示，如果该国 68 个受影响的卫生区中的任何一个能够追踪到如此高比例的实际暴露人数，他会感到“震惊”。

paras.en: “From what I’ve heard, pretty much everybody says contact tracing is nearly nonexistent in most of these places, and that’s why we’re having so much community death,” he says.
paras.zh: “据我所知，几乎每个人都说，这些地方的大多数地方几乎不存在接触者追踪，这就是为什么我们有如此多的社区死亡，”他说。

paras.en: Collecting data is difficult within extremely mobile populations affected by instability. The borders in central Africa are generally porous, and people are constantly traveling across them. The DRC is also facing severe insecurity marked by violent armed conflict across the country, which causes further displacement.
paras.zh: 在受不稳定影响的流动性极强的人群中收集数据非常困难。中非的边界普遍漏洞百出，人们不断穿越边界。刚果民主共和国还面临严重的不安全局势，全国各地的暴力武装冲突导致更多的流离失所。

paras.en: When just one infected person moves, it can start a new chain of transmission—and people are moving by the thousands, says the WHO’s Bélizaire. At the same time, there are more people living in dense urban centers, making the opportunity for spread even greater, she adds.
paras.zh: 世界卫生组织的贝利扎尔表示，只要一名感染者移动，就可能启动新的传播链，而且成千上万的人正在移动。她补充说，与此同时，越来越多的人生活在密集的城市中心，这使得传播的机会更大。

paras.en: If and when responders can get a fast-acting vaccine and a handle on contact tracing—and those are big ifs, experts warn—they face communities hardened by years of insecurity and distrust, says Joanne Liu, an epidemiologist at McGill University and former international president of Doctors Without Borders.
paras.zh: 麦吉尔大学流行病学家、无国界医生组织前国际主席乔安妮·刘 (Joanne Liu) 表示，如果救护人员能够获得速效疫苗并掌握接触者追踪的方法（专家警告说，这些都是很大的假设），他们将面临因多年不安全和不信任而变得僵硬的社区。

paras.en: Liu visited the DRC several times during a 2018–2019 Ebola outbreak and says she often heard from communities that they had bigger problems than the virus, including malaria, pneumonia, contaminated water and violent attacks. She calls the situation there a “mille-feuille context”—so full of layers and complexity that solutions must start and end with communities themselves.
paras.zh: 刘在2018年至2019年埃博拉疫情期间多次访问刚果民主共和国，她说她经常从社区听到，他们面临着比病毒更严重的问题，包括疟疾、肺炎、水污染和暴力袭击。她将那里的情况称为“千层酥的背景”——如此充满层次和复杂性，以至于解决方案必须从社区本身开始和结束。

paras.en: “What they see is a massive mobilization of aid coming for one specific disease, when actually their challenge is all of the other infectious diseases, plus the insecurity, and nobody is paying attention,” she says.
paras.zh: “他们看到的是针对一种特定疾病大规模动员援助，而实际上他们面临的挑战是所有其他传染病，加上不安全感，而且没有人关注，”她说。

paras.en: Liu worries that amid distrust and constant movement, the outbreak could spread farther to places such as the Central African Republic and South Sudan, which have little to no international public health infrastructure, making vaccination campaigns even more challenging.
paras.zh: 刘担心，在不信任和不断流动的情况下，疫情可能会进一步蔓延到中非共和国和南苏丹等地，这些国家几乎没有国际公共卫生基础设施，这使得疫苗接种活动变得更加困难。

paras.en: “It’s one thing to have a vaccine—it’s another thing that it transforms itself into a vaccination. A shot is only good once it’s in people’s arms,” she says.
paras.zh: “拥有疫苗是一回事，将其自身转化为疫苗接种则是另一回事。只有在人们手中注射疫苗才有用，”她说。

articles.title: Thanksgiving holiday travel could be disrupted by floods, winds and rain

paras.en: A series of poorly timed weather events from extreme floods to strong winds are slated to disrupt Thanksgiving travel this week across the U.S. East and West Coasts, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration forecasters say.
paras.zh: 美国国家海洋和大气管理局预报员表示，从极端洪水到强风等一系列不合时宜的天气事件预计将扰乱本周美国东海岸和西海岸的感恩节旅行。

paras.en: To the East, a storm is expected to dump at least 1.5 to two inches of rain on parts of Massachusetts, Connecticut, New York State, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland and Virginia between Wednesday and Friday, with up to four inches expected in areas of the Carolinas, according to the National Weather Service (NWS).
paras.zh: 据国家气象局 (NWS) 称，周三至周五，一场风暴预计将在东部马萨诸塞州、康涅狄格州、纽约州、新泽西州、特拉华州、马里兰州和弗吉尼亚州部分地区带来至少 1.5 至 2 英寸的降雨，卡罗莱纳州部分地区的降雨量预计将达到 4 英寸。

paras.en: Winds along the East Coast could exceed more than 50 miles per hour on the waterfront and 40 miles per hour inland over the same time, NWS says. If the prediction holds, there’s “likely to be some travel disruptions just based on those winds,” says Dave Radell, a meteorologist at the NWS’s New York City office.
paras.zh: NWS 表示，同一时间，东海岸海滨风速可能超过每小时 50 英里，内陆风速可能超过每小时 40 英里。美国国家气象局纽约市办事处的气象学家戴夫·拉德尔表示，如果预测成立，“可能会因为这些风而造成一些旅行中断”。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: Making matters worse, strong tides thanks to the sun’s and the moon’s pull could lead to “significant flooding and beach erosion” along the East Coast later this week, according to the NWS. The Saint Louis metro area might get a “sneaky, quick hit” of snow on Wednesday night, as the storm starts to “wind up,” says Joe Wegman, a meteorologist at NOAA’s Weather Prediction Center. But for the Northeast, “this is almost entirely a rainfall event.”
paras.zh: 更糟糕的是，据国家气象局称，由于太阳和月亮的引力，强烈的潮汐可能会导致本周晚些时候东海岸出现“严重的洪水和海滩侵蚀”。美国国家海洋和大气管理局 (NOAA) 天气预报中心的气象学家乔·韦格曼 (Joe Wegman) 表示，随着风暴开始“结束”，圣路易斯都市区可能会在周三晚上遭遇一场“偷偷摸摸的、快速的”降雪。但对于东北来说，“这几乎完全是一场降雨事件。”

paras.en: On the West Coast, strong tides, as well as a storm “well out” in the Pacific Ocean could help push water toward California, bringing significant flooding along parts of the coast, Wegman says. Parts of the San Francisco Bay Area could see as much as 2.7 feet of flooding above ground level this week, according to the NWS office in San Francisco.
paras.zh: 韦格曼说，在西海岸，强烈的潮汐以及太平洋上的风暴可能会将海水推向加利福尼亚州，从而给部分海岸带来严重的洪水。据 NWS 驻旧金山办事处称，本周旧金山湾区部分地区可能会出现地面以上 2.7 英尺的洪水。

paras.en: That flooding could affect homes, roadways and airports along the coast, says Dial Hoang, a meteorologist at the NWS’s Monterey, Calif., office. Two major airports in the region, San Francisco International Airport and Oakland San Francisco Bay Airport, are in coastal flood warning areas.
paras.zh: 美国国家气象局加利福尼亚州蒙特雷办事处的气象学家戴尔·黄（Dial Hoang）表示，洪水可能会影响沿海地区的房屋、道路和机场。该地区的两个主要机场旧金山国际机场和奥克兰旧金山湾机场均位于沿海洪水预警区。

paras.en: “We’ve been in close coordination with our government partners at both of the airports,” Hoang says. “They aware of the forecast implications, and they are taking mitigation steps to prevent disruptions to their operations.”
paras.zh: “我们一直与两个机场的政府合作伙伴密切协调，”黄说。 “他们意识到了预测的影响，并且正在采取缓解措施，以防止其运营中断。”

paras.en: For travelers, Wegman recommends keeping an eye on weather forecasts. In the New York region, “Thursday really looks like the brunt of things in terms of travel and in terms of impacts,” Radell says, so take that into consideration for your vacation plans, he says.
paras.zh: 对于旅行者，韦格曼建议留意天气预报。拉德尔说，在纽约地区，“从旅行和影响来看，周四确实是首当其冲的一天”，所以在你的假期计划中考虑到这一点。

paras.en: In areas where flooding is expected, residents should take precautions to protect flood-prone properties, Hoang advises. And if you come across a flooded road while driving—turn around.
paras.zh: 黄建议，在预计发生洪水的地区，居民应采取预防措施来保护易受洪水影响的财产。如果您在开车时遇到被洪水淹没的道路，请掉头。

articles.title: ‘Mitt & Ted’ recounts how a political odd couple changed U.S. health care
articles.author: Lily Burton

paras.en: In 1973, U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy often visited the cancer ward at Boston Children’s Hospital, where his eldest son was battling osteosarcoma. Kennedy witnessed other parents on the ward make impossible decisions regarding their child’s care when insurance didn’t cover it. Their stories lit a fire within the senator that burned bright for the rest of his life.
paras.zh: 1973年，美国参议员特德·肯尼迪经常探访波士顿儿童医院的癌症病房，他的大儿子正在那里与骨肉瘤作斗争。肯尼迪亲眼目睹了病房里的其他父母在保险不承保的情况下就孩子的护理做出了不可能的决定。他们的故事点燃了这位参议员内心的火焰，并在他的余生中熊熊燃烧。

paras.en: Kennedy spent decades fighting for health care reform, representing his home state of Massachusetts. He even teamed up with a former political rival from across the aisle: Mitt Romney. The story of this unexpected alliance is recounted in Mitt & Ted, the newest season of the GBH News podcast The Big Dig. Over eight episodes, journalist and host Ian Coss explores how their work laid the foundation for the Affordable Care Act, one of the most significant and divisive health care reforms in U.S. history.
paras.zh: 肯尼迪花了几十年时间代表他的家乡马萨诸塞州争取医疗改革。他甚至与来自两党的前政治对手米特·罗姆尼(Mitt Romney)合作。 GBH 新闻播客 The Big Dig 的最新一季《Mitt & Ted》讲述了这一意外联盟的故事。在八集中，记者兼主持人伊恩·科斯探讨了他们的工作如何为《平价医疗法案》奠定了基础，该法案是美国历史上最重要、最具争议性的医疗改革之一。

paras.en: We first meet Romney as a young upstart Republican challenger vying to flip Kennedy’s Senate seat in 1994. The race seemed close until a legendary debate. Romney had Kennedy on the defensive until the sitting senator pivoted to the issue near and dear to his heart: health care.
paras.zh: 我们第一次见到罗姆尼是在 1994 年，当时他是一位年轻的新贵共和党挑战者，正在争夺肯尼迪的参议院席位。这场竞选看起来很胶着，直到一场传奇般的辩论。罗姆尼让肯尼迪处于守势，直到现任参议员转向他最关心的问题：医疗保健。

paras.en: “Kennedy is the elder statesman, in command of the issue,” Coss says. “Romney is like an eager student trying to pass the test.” Using his deep knowledge, Kennedy buries the less experienced Romney. In the election, Kennedy then beat Romney by a landslide, even when many Democrats were ousted by Republican challengers that same year. But the loss may have motivated Romney to keep going.
paras.zh: “肯尼迪是年长的政治家，负责解决这个问题，”科斯说。 “罗姆尼就像一个渴望通过考试的学生。”肯尼迪利用他深厚的知识埋葬了经验不足的罗姆尼。在选举中，肯尼迪以压倒性优势击败了罗姆尼，尽管同年许多民主党人被共和党挑战者赶下台。但这次失败可能激励罗姆尼继续前进。

paras.en: Several years later, Romney unexpectedly became a champion of health care reform as the newly elected governor of Massachusetts. The state’s health care system was facing the potential loss of about a billion dollars in federal funding, threatening hospitals that served vulnerable populations. Romney’s administration created Romneycare, which was supported by three features: individual and employer mandates, affordable options for low-income people, and a health care exchange where people could compare plans from different providers.
paras.zh: 几年后，罗姆尼出人意料地成为医疗改革的倡导者，成为新当选的马萨诸塞州州长。该州的医疗保健系统可能面临约 10 亿美元联邦资金的损失，威胁到为弱势群体提供服务的医院。罗姆尼政府创建了罗姆尼医保，它具有三个特点：个人和雇主的强制要求、低收入人群负担得起的选择以及医疗保健交换，人们可以在其中比较不同提供者的计划。

paras.en: With Senator Kennedy’s help, the groundbreaking law passed in 2006 and expanded health insurance coverage to 98 percent of Massachusetts’ population.
paras.zh: 在肯尼迪参议员的帮助下，这项开创性的法律于 2006 年获得通过，将医疗保险覆盖范围扩大到马萨诸塞州 98% 的人口。

paras.en: Romneycare gained national attention and kicked off years-long efforts to replicate it on the federal level. Finally, in 2010, President Obama signed the Affordable Care Act, or ACA. Modeled on Romneycare, the law (colloquially called Obamacare) adapted the reforms made in Massachusetts for all 50 states, a challenge since many states had larger shares of uninsured people than Massachusetts had even before Romneycare.
paras.zh: 罗姆尼医改引起了全国的关注，并开始了长达数年的努力，以在联邦层面复制它。最后，2010 年，奥巴马总统签署了平价医疗法案 (ACA)。该法律（俗称奥巴马医改）以罗姆尼医改为蓝本，将马萨诸塞州的改革适用于所有 50 个州，这是一项挑战，因为许多州没有保险的人口比例甚至比罗姆尼医改之前的马萨诸塞州还要高。

paras.en: The Democrats in Congress also sought to include a government insurance plan in the reform, similar to Medicaid but available to more people. Republicans were wary of the ACA generally, but a government-provided insurance option was a line they wouldn’t cross. The ACA eventually passed without the public option, but by then the political winds had shifted. If there ever was a chance to secure bipartisan support for the law, it was gone by the time Democrats were willing to compromise on the public option. And as soon as the ACA became law, Republicans started fighting it.
paras.zh: 国会民主党人还寻求在改革中纳入政府保险计划，类似于医疗补助计划，但可供更多人使用。共和党人总体上对《平价医疗法案》持谨慎态度，但政府提供的保险选项是他们不会跨越的界限。 《平价医疗法案》最终在没有公众选择的情况下获得通过，但那时政治风向已经发生了转变。如果说曾经有机会获得两党对这项法律的支持，那么当民主党愿意在公众选择上妥协时，这个机会就已经消失了。 《平价医疗法案》一成为法律，共和党人就开始与之抗争。

paras.en: The podcast traces an impressive number of political twists and turns on this health care reform journey. Though I got turned around a few times, I never fully lost the plot thanks to Coss’ well-placed reminders and takeaways.
paras.zh: 该播客追溯了这一医疗改革之旅中令人印象深刻的政治曲折。尽管我被转了好几次，但多亏了科斯的恰到好处的提醒和要点，我从未完全失去了情节。

paras.en: Beyond the story of Romney and Kennedy, the podcast gives voice to many more people who made the ACA a reality: government workers who went from foes to allies who enlisted unlikely help from the conservative Heritage Foundation; longtime friends in the Massachusetts state legislature who were driven apart by the reform; a father who struggled to afford health care and how he advocated for reform with his church. I teared up more than once listening to the human stories behind these policy changes.
paras.zh: 除了罗姆尼和肯尼迪的故事之外，播客还讲述了更多使 ACA 成为现实的人的声音：从敌人变成盟友的政府工作人员，他们从保守的传统基金会那里获得了意想不到的帮助；马萨诸塞州立法机关的老朋友因改革而疏远；一位为支付医疗费用而苦苦挣扎的父亲，以及他如何与教会一起倡导改革。我不止一次在听着这些政策变化背后的人性故事时落泪。

paras.en: Overall, Mitt & Ted gave me new appreciation for why passing a reform is so difficult, despite how life-changing and life-saving access to health care can be. The series points to moments when stars aligned to make reform possible and suggests that more of those opportunities lie ahead.
paras.zh: 总体而言，米特和泰德让我重新认识到为什么通过一项改革如此困难，尽管获得医疗保健可以改变生活并挽救生命。该系列节目指出了众星齐心协力使改革成为可能的时刻，并表明未来还有更多这样的机会。

paras.en: “The work of American health care remains very much unfinished,” Coss says. “When the perfect alignment of frustration and opportunity arrives again, that might be what determines whether our leaders actually work together.”
paras.zh: “美国医疗保健的工作仍未完成，”科斯说。 “当挫折与机遇完美结合时，这可能决定我们的领导人是否真正合作。”

articles.title: The notion of ‘positive masculinity’ is dividing the male studies field
articles.author: Sujata Gupta

paras.en: Ryon McDermott set out seven years ago to create a new scale measuring masculinity. McDermott, along with other researchers studying male psyches, was tired of the field’s long-standing assertion that the manlier the man, the worse his outcomes. It was high time to measure masculinity in a positive light.
paras.zh: 瑞恩·麦克德莫特七年前开始着手创建一种新的衡量男性气质的量表。麦克德莫特和其他研究男性心理的研究人员厌倦了该领域长期以来的主张，即男人越有男子气概，他的结果就越糟糕。是时候从积极的角度来衡量男性气质了。

paras.en: For almost half a century, the many social science scales that measure gender or masculinity have consistently shown that rigid fealty to Western masculine norms — such as prioritizing work, power-seeking and status — link with poor mental and physical health. Endorsement of such norms also correlates with misogynistic beliefs and violent behaviors, including sexual violence, studies have shown.
paras.zh: 近半个世纪以来，许多衡量性别或男性气质的社会科学量表一致表明，对西方男性规范的严格忠诚——例如优先考虑工作、追求权力和地位——与不良的心理和身体健康有关。研究表明，对此类规范的认可也与厌恶女性的信仰和暴力行为（包括性暴力）相关。

paras.en: But giving men a talking-to about their many defects rarely lands well. Nor does that negative focus help men thrive. But what approach would help? “We don’t really have a definition of men’s health. If we don’t know what we are going towards, how can we even do this [research]?” says Matt Englar-Carlson, a counseling expert at California State University, Fullerton.
paras.zh: 但与男人谈论他们的许多缺陷很少能取得好的效果。这种消极的关注也无助于男性的成长。但什么方法会有帮助呢？ “我们对男性健康并没有真正的定义。如果我们不知道我们的目标是什么，我们怎么能进行这项[研究]呢？”加州州立大学富勒顿分校的咨询专家马特·恩格拉尔-卡尔森说。

paras.en: What traits, the researchers wondered, define a healthy man? And could a healthy reframing of manhood improve men’s outcomes, such as by getting them to the doctor or lowering their high rates of social isolation, depression and even death by suicide?
paras.zh: 研究人员想知道什么特征可以定义一个健康的男人？健康地重塑男子气概是否可以改善男性的健康状况，例如让他们去看医生或降低他们的高社会孤立率、抑郁症甚至自杀死亡率？

paras.en: Those questions would cleave the field, though as fights go, this one has been downright nice. McDermott, a psychologist of masculinity at the University of South Alabama in Mobile, would ultimately question positive masculinity’s very existence. Meanwhile, his friends and collaborators at Movember — a nonprofit research organization based in Richmond, Australia that encourages mustache-growing in November to spark conversations around men’s health issues — are poised for a 2027 launch of the Healthy Manhood Index. That scale uses a positive framing and is designed to gauge men’s strengths, while illuminating areas for improvement.
paras.zh: 这些问题将会分裂这个领域，尽管随着战斗的进行，这一场比赛已经非常精彩了。麦克德莫特是南阿拉巴马大学莫比尔分校的男性气质心理学家，他最终质疑积极男性气质的存在。与此同时，他在 Movember 的朋友和合作者准备在 2027 年推出健康男子气概指数。 Movember 是一家位于澳大利亚里士满的非营利性研究组织，鼓励人们在 11 月留胡子，以引发围绕男性健康问题的对话。该量表采用积极的框架，旨在衡量男性的优势，同时指出需要改进的领域。

paras.en: Masculinity is treated as a barrier to health
paras.zh: 男性气质被视为健康的障碍

paras.en: The first gender measurement scale emerged almost a century ago. It positioned femininity and masculinity at opposite poles, with researchers assuming that the most gender-conforming men and women were the healthiest.
paras.zh: 第一个性别测量量表出现于近一个世纪前。它将女性气质和男性气质置于相反的两极，研究人员认为最符合性别的男性和女性是最健康的。

paras.en: That thinking has since unraveled. As women began smashing gender barriers, by doing everything from donning pants to entering the workforce, penalties for women acting more masculine largely disappeared.
paras.zh: 这种想法后来被瓦解了。随着女性开始打破性别障碍，从穿裤子到进入劳动力市场，对表现得更男性化的女性的惩罚基本上消失了。

paras.en: Inspired by the feminist movement, researchers began studying the masculine psyche. Yet they largely framed masculinity as a barrier to health. The Male Role Norms Inventory, one of the most popular masculinity scales in use today, exemplifies that focus. Individuals rank statements like: “A man must stand on his own two feet and never depend on other people to help him do things.”
paras.zh: 受到女权主义运动的启发，研究人员开始研究男性心理。然而，他们在很大程度上将男性气质视为健康的障碍。男性角色规范清单是当今最流行的男性气概量表之一，它体现了这一重点。人们常说：“一个人必须靠自己的两只脚站起来，永远不要依赖别人帮助他做事。”

paras.en: The higher the score on that and more than 60 similar statements appearing in popular masculinity scales used over the past 50 or so years, the worse men’s outcomes, McDermott and his colleagues at Movember reported in July in Men and Masculinities. “Manlier” men often struggle with depression and substance use and engage in sexual aggression. They also tend to avoid asking for help or taking precautionary health measures, such as wearing a mask during the COVID-19 pandemic.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特和他在 Movember 的同事 7 月在《男性与男性气概》杂志上报告称，在过去 50 多年使用的流行男性气概量表中，得分越高，男性的结果就越差。 “有男子气概”的男人经常与抑郁症和药物滥用作斗争，并进行性侵犯。他们还倾向于避免寻求帮助或采取预防性健康措施，例如在 COVID-19 大流行期间戴口罩。

paras.en: But almost 80 percent of the statements used frame masculinity as a problem to be solved, the team found. That deficit lens biases the findings, argues coauthor and social psychologist Peter Fisher of the Movember Institute of Men’s Health, the organization’s research arm. “If the only tools you have available to you are looking for deficits, you will find deficits,” says Fisher, who is based in Santa Monica, Calif.
paras.zh: 但研究小组发现，近 80% 的陈述将框架男性气概视为需要解决的问题。该组织研究机构莫维贝尔男性健康研究所的合著者、社会心理学家彼得·费舍尔认为，这种缺陷视角会导致研究结果产生偏差。 “如果你可用的唯一工具就是寻找赤字，你就会发现赤字，”住在加利福尼亚州圣莫尼卡的费舍尔说。

paras.en: Researchers pivot to studying positive masculinity
paras.zh: 研究人员转向研究积极的男性气质

paras.en: That negative framing has also seeped into public discourse, so much so that some people now intuitively link “masculinity” with the word “toxic.”
paras.zh: 这种负面框架也渗透到了公共话语中，以至于一些人现在直觉地将“男子气概”与“有毒”一词联系起来。

paras.en: Yet those most macho of men are the outliers, the small percentage who score highest on masculinity scales, Englar-Carlson says. He suspects that what really matters for health is flexibility around when to behave in certain ways. Stoicism, a typically masculine-coded trait, can be calming in emergencies but scary when a man experiences a mental health crisis and refuses help.
paras.zh: 然而，恩格拉-卡尔森说，那些最具男子气概的男性却是异类，即在男子气概量表上得分最高的一小部分人。他怀疑对健康真正重要的是何时以某种方式行事的灵活性。斯多葛主义是一种典型的男性特征，在紧急情况下可以让人平静，但当一个男人经历心理健康危机并拒绝帮助时，它就会令人恐惧。

paras.en: Englar-Carlson and psychologist Mark Kiselica, of Penn State University, Harrisburg, developed the Positive Psychology Positive Masculinity, or PPPM, paradigm in 2010. Public health experts, therapists and others should focus on men’s strengths not deficits, they argued.
paras.zh: 恩格拉尔-卡尔森和哈里斯堡宾夕法尼亚州立大学的心理学家马克·基塞利卡于 2010 年开发了积极心理学积极男子气概（PPPM）范式。他们认为，公共卫生专家、治疗师和其他人应该关注男性的优势而不是缺陷。

paras.en: The ideas in PPPM are what McDermott began trying to turn into a masculinity scale a few years later. But his efforts sent him into a tailspin.
paras.zh: 几年后，麦克德莫特开始尝试将 PPPM 中的想法转化为男性气质量表。但他的努力却让他陷入了困境。

paras.en: He and his colleagues began by identifying positive traits that people linked more with men than women. The team generated a list of 79 possible positive male attributes based on findings from focus groups and studies of positive masculinity and positive psychology, such as “having a good sense of humor,” “serving country or community” and “having passion for one’s work.” More than 1,000 individuals then rated those attributes on a scale from 1 for “strongly disagree” to 7 for “strongly agree” along three dimensions: positive, typically expected of men and typically expected of women.
paras.zh: 他和他的同事首先确定了人们更容易与男性而非女性联系在一起的积极特征。该团队根据焦点小组的调查结果以及积极男子气概和积极心理学的研究，列出了 79 种可能的积极男性特质，例如“有良好的幽默感”、“为国家或社区服务”和“对自己的工作充满热情”。然后，超过 1,000 人根据三个维度对这些属性进行评分，从 1（“强烈不同意”）到 7（“强烈同意”）：积极、通常对男性的期望和通常对女性的期望。

paras.en: Roughly 40 percent of the attributes, particularly those pertaining to protective behaviors and assertiveness, were seen as both positive and expected more of men than of women, McDermott and his colleagues reported in 2019 in Psychology of Men & Masculinities.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特和他的同事在 2019 年《男性与男性气质心理学》中报告称，大约 40% 的特质，特别是那些与保护行为和自信相关的特质，被认为是男性比女性更积极且更值得期待的特质。

paras.en: But the study also showed that both men and women scored above the midpoint on almost all the allegedly male attributes. That could mean the supposedly gendered attributes had little to do with gender. And for many measures, such as patience and having good hygiene, women scored higher than men. Could that mean that the study’s list was rebranding attributes from feminism as masculine? The idea didn’t sit well with McDermott.
paras.zh: 但研究还表明，男性和女性在几乎所有所谓的男性属性上的得分都高于中点。这可能意味着所谓的性别属性与性别几乎没有关系。在许多指标上，例如耐心和良好的卫生习惯，女性的得分高于男性。这是否意味着该研究的清单将女权主义的属性重新标记为男性特征？麦克德莫特并不认同这个想法。

paras.en: Then, the team’s research took a dark turn. The researchers had respondents fill out both their new masculinity survey and a scale measuring sexist beliefs. That revealed that the more strongly respondents endorsed masculine ideals, the more likely they were to endorse sexist beliefs, the team’s unpublished work shows. Think about a statement like, “A good man should be strong,” McDermott says. For many people, that translates to “a good woman should be weak.”
paras.zh: 然后，团队的研究出现了黑暗的转折。研究人员让受访者填写新的男性气质调查和衡量性别歧视信念的量表。该团队未发表的研究表明，这表明受访者越强烈地支持男性理想，他们就越有可能支持性别歧视信仰。想想这样一句话：“一个好人应该坚强，”麦克德莫特说。对于很多人来说，这意味着“好女人应该是软弱的”。

paras.en: “I’ve looked at this across three different samples [of people], and I find the same results each time,” McDermott says. “Whenever you define masculinity, you are inherently defining it against femininity.”
paras.zh: “我对三个不同的[人]样本进行了研究，每次都发现相同的结果，”麦克德莫特说。 “每当你定义男性气质时，你本质上就是在针对女性气质来定义它。”

paras.en: Most attributes are neither male nor female, but human, McDermott has come to believe. And gendering those universal traits merely reinforces sexist stereotypes. The work has left him gutted. “I really thought that there was such thing as positive masculinity,” he says. “But now I believe that it can never truly be positive.”
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特开始相信，大多数属性既不是男性也不是女性，而是人类。而对这些普遍特征进行性别化只会强化性别歧视的刻板印象。这项工作让他心灰意冷。 “我真的认为存在积极的男子气概，”他说。 “但现在我相信它永远不可能真正是积极的。”

paras.en: Fisher is well aware of McDermott’s journey. “He’s been trying to create a positive masculinity scale, or isolate the positive characteristics of masculinity, for a while,” Fisher says. “And he’s been struggling.”
paras.zh: 费舍尔非常了解麦克德莫特的旅程。 “一段时间以来，他一直在尝试创建一个积极的男性气概量表，或者孤立男性气概的积极特征，”费舍尔说。 “而且他一直在挣扎。”

paras.en: Perhaps McDermott has set too high a bar, Fisher says. Rather than trying to identify and measure masculinity through beliefs, he says, why not focus on men’s actions?
paras.zh: 费舍尔说，也许麦克德莫特设定的标准太高了。他说，与其试图通过信仰来识别和衡量男性气质，为什么不关注男性的行为呢？

paras.en: So for the past several years, Fisher and colleagues have been doing just that. They have organized numerous focus groups and tested survey statements with some 12,000 individuals across six countries. Besides addressing the lack of age and cultural diversity used to create most masculinity scales currently in use, Fisher and his team hope that their scale will provide men with a blueprint for what constitutes healthy behavior.
paras.zh: 所以在过去的几年里，费舍尔和他的同事一直在这样做。他们组织了许多焦点小组，并对来自六个国家的约 12,000 人的调查陈述进行了测试。除了解决目前使用的大多数男性气质量表缺乏年龄和文化多样性的问题外，费舍尔和他的团队希望他们的量表能为男性提供健康行为的蓝图。

paras.en: Here’s what a healthy masculinity index might measure
paras.zh: 以下是健康男性气质指数的衡量标准

paras.en: Below are qualities Movember Institute of Men’s Health researchers are evaluating to develop a new masculinity scale. The items are preliminary and may not appear in the final version. The rows show counterproductive behaviors that result from pressures facing men, healthy responses and possible wording for survey statements the men would then rate.
paras.zh: Movember 男性健康研究所的研究人员正在评估以下品质，以开发新的男性气质量表。这些项目是初步的，可能不会出现在最终版本中。这些争吵显示出适得其反的行为，这些行为是由男性面临的压力、健康的反应以及男性随后评分的调查陈述的可能措辞造成的。

paras.en: All the statements in the Healthy Manhood Index start with “I” plus a verb, such as “I do,” “I talk” or “I check in,” Fisher says. For instance, men often feel pressure to restrict their emotions, so the healthy response would be for men to open up emotionally. The index might have men rate a statement like: “I share difficult things I’m going through with people I trust.” Crucially, the higher the score on the index, the healthier the man.
paras.zh: 费舍尔说，健康男子气概指数中的所有陈述都以“我”加动词开头，例如“我做”、“我说话”或“我签到”。例如，男性经常感到有压力去限制自己的情绪，因此健康的反应是男性在情感上敞开心扉。该指数可能会让男性对这样的陈述进行评分：“我与我信任的人分享我正在经历的困难事情。”至关重要的是，该指数得分越高，男人就越健康。

paras.en: Fisher’s goal is to move men toward healthy behaviors without alienating them. “We just want to meet men where they are,” he says.
paras.zh: 费舍尔的目标是在不疏远男性的情况下引导他们采取健康的行为。 “我们只是想在人们所在的地方认识他们，”他说。

paras.en: Should researchers keep or toss masculinity?
paras.zh: 研究人员应该保留还是放弃男性气质？

paras.en: A debate that could easily become acrimonious has remained almost cloyingly friendly. McDermott refers to Fisher as “brilliant.” Fisher credits McDermott for “letting the data change his mind.”
paras.zh: 一场很容易变得激烈的辩论却保持着近乎令人厌烦的友好。麦克德莫特称费舍尔“才华横溢”。费舍尔称赞麦克德莫特“让数据改变了他的想法”。

paras.en: Researchers in the field recognize that they share the same goals, says psychological researcher Michael Addis of Clark University in Worcester, Mass. They want men to be healthier and to treat others, including women and seemingly less masculine men, with respect. “The question is how do we do that? We either sell them on a new masculinity, or we say ‘…. masculinity is always going to be in some ways a box,’” he says.
paras.zh: 马萨诸塞州伍斯特克拉克大学的心理学研究员迈克尔·阿迪斯表示，该领域的研究人员认识到他们有着相同的目标。他们希望男性更健康，并尊重他人，包括女性和看似不那么阳刚的男性。 “问题是我们该如何做到这一点？我们要么向他们推销一种新的男子气概，要么我们说‘……男子气概在某些方面永远是一个盒子，’”他说。

paras.en: Though discussions around how to frame masculinity can feel wonky, the stakes are real, Addis and psychiatrist and behavioral scientist Ethan Hoffmann of Stanford University wrote in 2024 in Psychology of Men & Masculinities.
paras.zh: 艾迪斯和斯坦福大学的精神病学家和行为科学家伊桑·霍夫曼 (Ethan Hoffmann) 在 2024 年的《男性与男性气质心理学》中写道，尽管围绕如何构建男性气质的讨论可能会让人感觉不太靠谱，但其中的利害关系却是真实存在的。

paras.en: Consider suicide. Men who strongly endorsed masculine norms were less likely than others to seek help for depression and more likely to die by suicide, researchers reported in 2025 in Psychiatry International.
paras.zh: 考虑自杀。研究人员于 2025 年在《国际精神病学》杂志上报告称，强烈支持男性规范的男性比其他人更不可能寻求抑郁症帮助，而且更有可能自杀身亡。

paras.en: Theoretically, public health campaigns aimed at men can help. But what form should they take? A positive masculinity campaign may recast a statement like, “real men never ask for help” to “real men know when it’s time to ask for help,” Addis and Hoffman write. But a campaign that rejects gender labels may roll out statements like: “Real men aren’t real: It’s a fiction that could cost you your life.”
paras.zh: 从理论上讲，针对男性的公共卫生运动可以有所帮助。但它们应该采取什么形式呢？阿迪斯和霍夫曼写道，一场积极的男子气概运动可能会将“真正的男人从不寻求帮助”这样的说法改写为“真正的男人知道什么时候该寻求帮助”。但拒绝性别标签的运动可能会推出这样的声明：“真正的男人并不真实：这是一个可能会让你丧命的虚构故事。”

paras.en: Such postgender messaging may feel too abstract for the average guy, Fisher says. Convincing a 65-year-old man to stay on top of his prostate cancer appointments is hard enough without trying to shift his worldview.
paras.zh: 费舍尔说，这种后性别信息对于普通人来说可能感觉太抽象了。如果不试图改变一名 65 岁的男性的世界观，说服他继续做好前列腺癌的预约就已经够困难的了。

paras.en: McDermott counters that positive masculinity “makes the sex role stuff continue,” enshrining the idea that gender roles and hierarchies constitute a necessary organizing principle for societies.
paras.zh: 麦克德莫特反驳说，积极的男子气概“让性别角色的东西继续存在”，并坚信性别角色和等级制度构成了社会必要的组织原则。

paras.en: Reconciliation may be possible, Addis says. Policy makers and public health experts could first rope men in with a more positive masculine approach. Then over time, they could help men question and relinquish gender norms. “I call it dancing with the devil,” or temporarily adopting the gendered approach as a means to a desired end, he says.
paras.zh: 阿迪斯说，和解是可能的。政策制定者和公共卫生专家可以首先以更积极的男性方式吸引男性参与。然后随着时间的推移，它们可以帮助男性质疑并放弃性别规范。他说，“我称之为与魔鬼共舞”，或者暂时采用性别化的方式作为达到预期目的的手段。

paras.en: However the debate unfurls, researchers are writing their own script on how to fight like real men — or real people. “There’s a lot of men in the psychology of men [field] who have worked really hard to not let our egos get in the way of good work,” Addis says. “It’s sort of like practice what you preach.”
paras.zh: 无论争论如何展开，研究人员正在编写自己的脚本，讲述如何像真正的男人或真正的人一样战斗。 “在男性心理学领域，有很多男性非常努力地工作，不让我们的自负妨碍我们做好工作，”阿迪斯说。 “这有点像言行一致。”

paras.en: If you or someone you care about may be at risk of suicide, the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline offers free, 24/7 support, information and local resources from trained counselors. Call or text 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org.
paras.zh: 如果您或您关心的人可能有自杀风险，988 自杀和危机生命热线可提供来自训练有素的咨询师的免费 24/7 支持、信息和本地资源。致电或发短信 988 或通过 988lifeline.org 聊天。

articles.title: Math’s holy grail, the Riemann hypothesis, appears solved with AI’s help
articles.author: Kathryn Hulick

paras.en: A long-sought pinnacle of mathematics has apparently been reached. In a feat that will go down in mathematics history, a human working with AI appears to have solved the most famous puzzle in math, proving the Riemann hypothesis. The problem has foiled repeated and valiant attempts at solution for more than a century.
paras.zh: 显然已经达到了长期寻求的数学顶峰。人类与人工智能的合作似乎已经解决了最著名的数学难题，证明了黎曼猜想，这是一项将载入数学史册的壮举。一个多世纪以来，人们多次勇敢地尝试解决这个问题，但都失败了。

paras.en: Now, mathematicians are working to understand the proof, posted by Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, on November 20. The Riemann hypothesis, if true, reveals the secrets of prime numbers. In a statement on his website, Alpöge said he’d developed the proof alongside Anthropic’s AI tool Claude.
paras.zh: 现在，数学家们正在努力理解 Anthropic 数学家 Levent Alpöge 于 11 月 20 日发布的证明。如果黎曼假设成立，它将揭示素数的秘密。 Alpöge 在其网站上的一份声明中表示，他与 Anthropic 的人工智能工具 Claude 一起开发了证明。

paras.en: By the next day, independent mathematicians had confirmed the result. “We have full confidence that Alpöge’s proof of the Riemann hypothesis is correct, and we congratulate him on this achievement,” read a joint statement from Lean Focused Research Organization and Mathlib Initiative.
paras.zh: 第二天，独立数学家证实了这一结果。 “我们完全相信 Alpöge 对黎曼假设的证明是正确的，我们祝贺他取得这一成就，”精益聚焦研究组织和 Mathlib Initiative 的联合声明中写道。

paras.en: A proof of the Riemann hypothesis is one of the most sought after achievements in mathematics. “As a mathematical landmark, it really doesn’t get bigger than this. I can’t think of a theorem proven not only in my lifetime, maybe in the history of mathematics that is as important as this,” says mathematician Ken Ono of Axiom Math and the University of Virginia in Charlottesville.
paras.zh: 黎曼猜想的证明是数学界最受追捧的成就之一。 “作为一个数学里程碑，它真的没有比这更伟大的了。我想不出一个不仅在我有生之年得到证明的定理，也许在数学史上也如此重要，”Axiom Math 和夏洛茨维尔弗吉尼亚大学的数学家肯·小野 (Ken Ono) 说道。

paras.en: “It’s an historic achievement,” says Bryna Kra, a mathematician at Northwestern University in Evanston, Ill.
paras.zh: “这是一项历史性的成就，”伊利诺伊州埃文斯顿西北大学的数学家布赖娜·克拉 (Bryna Kra) 说。

paras.en: Importantly, this was not the work of AI alone, Kra says. First of all, Claude had been trained on the work of thousands of human mathematicians, plus Alpöge was an experienced mathematician himself. He did not just ask for the proof then “push a button and wait,” Kra says.
paras.zh: 克拉说，重要的是，这不仅仅是人工智能的工作。首先，克劳德接受过数千名人类数学家工作的培训，而且阿尔波格本人也是一位经验丰富的数学家。克拉说，他不只是要求提供证据，然后“按下按钮然后等待”。

paras.en: Over six weeks, he worked back and forth with Claude. As an AI agent, Claude can use outside tools to perform tasks. The precise version of Claude that Alpöge used has not been disclosed, but the AI checked its work using Lean, software that converts mathematical arguments into code in order to confirm that a chain of logic holds up. It also had access to Mathlib, a library of known arguments already converted into Lean.
paras.zh: 六个星期以来，他与克劳德一起工作。作为人工智能代理，克劳德可以使用外部工具来执行任务。 Alpöge 使用的 Claude 的精确版本尚未公开，但人工智能使用 Lean 检查其工作，该软件将数学参数转换为代码，以确认逻辑链是否成立。它还可以访问 Mathlib，这是一个已经转换为 Lean 的已知参数库。

paras.en: The result is 250,000 pages of dense, complex math. The world’s mathematicians are still working to translate the proof into a form people can understand. “What’s amazing about this proof is that it involves so many different areas of mathematics,” Ono says. “And I don’t know how a single human being could hold all of the ideas in their mind.”
paras.zh: 结果是 250,000 页的密集、复杂的数学。世界上的数学家仍在努力将证明转化为人们可以理解的形式。 “这个证明的惊人之处在于它涉及数学的许多不同领域，”小野说。 “我不知道一个人怎么能把所有的想法都记在脑子里。”

paras.en: The Riemann hypothesis, which dates to 1859, is closely linked with prime numbers. Prime numbers seem to be sprinkled randomly along the number line, but the Riemann hypothesis reveals a hidden order. At play is a mathematical enigma called the Riemann zeta function. The zeros of this function — the values that, when plugged into the function, produce a zero — are closely related to prime numbers. The Riemann hypothesis says that certain zeros — of which there are an infinite number — all sit on a particular line on a graph. If that is true, it would reveal how many primes exist below a given number.
paras.zh: 黎曼猜想可以追溯到 1859 年，它与素数密切相关。素数似乎沿着数轴随机散布，但黎曼假设揭示了隐藏的顺序。起作用的是一个称为黎曼 zeta 函数的数学谜题。该函数的零点（当插入该函数时产生零的值）与素数密切相关。黎曼假设指出，某些零（其中有无限多个）都位于图上的特定线上。如果这是真的，它将揭示给定数字以下存在多少个素数。

paras.en: Because so much of mathematics involves prime numbers, many other mathematical statements rest on the correctness of the hypothesis. The new proof will have wide implications. “It’s an earthquake throughout mathematics,” Ono says.
paras.zh: 由于许多数学涉及素数，因此许多其他数学陈述都依赖于假设的正确性。新的证明将产生广泛的影响。 “这是整个数学界的一场地震，”小野说。

paras.en: Alpöge claims to have solved not only the Riemann hypothesis itself, but a more general form of it, called the generalized Riemann hypothesis, which extends the idea to related functions. Though he guided the AI, Alpöge wrote that “what I saw during the course of progress so amazed me that I believe it is one dawn across science of something far greater … Claude far outpaced me near the finish line.”
paras.zh: Alpöge 声称不仅解决了黎曼假设本身，而且还解决了它的更一般形式，称为广义黎曼假设，它将这一想法扩展到相关函数。尽管阿尔波格是人工智能的指导者，但他写道，“我在进展过程中所看到的一切让我感到非常惊讶，我相信这是科学界的一个黎明，它的意义要大得多……克劳德在终点线附近远远超过了我。”

paras.en: AI has been steadily felling major problems of mathematics, and this is the biggest one yet. But according to cognitive scientist Gary Marcus of New York University, AI’s genius at math will not carry over to more open-ended types of problems in biology, business or robotics. “In short, it’s not at all obvious that whatever Alpöge did has the generality many people are hoping for,” he wrote in a Substack post.
paras.zh: 人工智能一直在稳步解决数学的重大问题，这是迄今为止最大的一个。但根据纽约大学认知科学家加里·马库斯的说法，人工智能在数学方面的天赋不会延续到生物学、商业或机器人技术等更开放式的问题类型上。 “简而言之，无论 Alpöge 所做的事情是否具有许多人所希望的普遍性，这一点并不明显，”他在 Substack 帖子中写道。

paras.en: And some mathematicians have pushed back against the dominance of AI, disputing the utility of proofs created with the technology. The Association for Human Mathematics wrote in a November 20 statement on their website that no human being can claim to be responsible for the Riemann hypothesis proof, and that no mathematician can “confirm with full certainty that the proof is correct.”
paras.zh: 一些数学家反对人工智能的主导地位，质疑该技术创建的证明的效用。人类数学协会在其网站上11月20日的一份声明中写道，没有人可以声称自己对黎曼假设的证明负责，也没有数学家可以“完全确定地证实证明是正确的”。

paras.en: Kra has been critical of achievements where AI agents worked largely on their own, independent of human intervention. The recent solution, by OpenAI, to a puzzle about the Navier-Stokes equations that describe fluids came about that way. But Alpöge’s approach was different, Kra says. “There is someone to stand behind [the work],” she says. She just hopes that people don’t see this as an end to math. “I think that this is a beginning, this is opening up more questions than it answers. … I think we have to use our imagination and find what’s the next frontier.”
paras.zh: 克拉一直对人工智能代理在很大程度上独立于人类干预而独立工作的成就持批评态度。 OpenAI 最近提出的关于描述流体的纳维-斯托克斯方程难题的解决方案就是通过这种方式实现的。但克拉说，阿尔波格的方法有所不同。 “[工作]背后有人支持，”她说。她只是希望人们不要认为这是数学的终结。 “我认为这是一个开始，它提出的问题多于答案。……我认为我们必须发挥我们的想象力，找到下一个前沿领域。”

articles.title: DNA From The Shroud of Turin Reveals a Surprise Centuries Later
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: The Shroud of Turin has had a long and fascinating history since its existence was first recorded in historical documents in 1354, and there continues to be plenty of debate around what exactly this ancient artifact is.
paras.zh: 自 1354 年历史文献首次记录都灵裹尸布的存在以来，都灵裹尸布有着悠久而迷人的历史，而关于这件古代文物到底是什么，仍然存在着大量争论。

paras.en: A study published in Scientific Reports represents the most thorough DNA analysis of the Shroud to date, with an international team of researchers tracking all of the available genetic evidence that has settled on the cloth over the ages.
paras.zh: 《科学报告》中发表的一项研究代表了迄今为止对裹尸布最彻底的 DNA 分析，国际研究小组追踪了多年来在裹尸布上发现的所有可用遗传证据。

paras.en: While the analysis doesn't tell us if this fabric was once wrapped around the body of Jesus or not, it does tell us more about the journey it's been on, and the effects that human repair and handling have had on it.
paras.zh: 虽然分析没有告诉我们这种织物是否曾经包裹过耶稣的尸体，但它确实告诉我们更多关于它所经历的旅程，以及人类修复和处理对其产生的影响。

paras.en: "The Shroud represents a rich archive of genetic information that has accumulated over centuries of human interaction and environmental exposure," says forensic scientist Noemi Procopio, from the University of Lancashire in the UK.
paras.zh: 英国兰开夏大学法医科学家诺埃米·普罗科皮奥 (Noemi Procopio) 表示：“裹尸布代表了一个丰富的遗传信息档案，这些信息是几个世纪以来人类互动和环境暴露所积累的。”

paras.en: While DNA tests have been carried out on the cloth before, here the researchers went several steps further with a PCR-free, next-generation metagenomic sequencing method.
paras.zh: 虽然之前已经在布料上进行过 DNA 测试，但研究人员在这里更进一步，采用了无 PCR 的下一代宏基因组测序方法。

paras.en: PCR-free means there was no artificial copying of DNA fragments (via a method called polymerase chain reaction), reducing the likelihood of bias.
paras.zh: 无 PCR 意味着不存在 DNA 片段的人工复制（通过称为聚合酶链式反应的方法），从而减少了偏差的可能性。

paras.en: Add in those other technical terms – the next-generation aspect (reading millions of DNA fragments in parallel), and the metagenomic approach (looking for DNA from any kind of organism rather than a single one), and you can see why it's more comprehensive than previous tests.
paras.zh: 再加上其他技术术语——下一代方面（并行读取数百万个 DNA 片段）和宏基因组方法（从任何种类的生物体而不是单一生物体中寻找 DNA），您就会明白为什么它比以前的测试更全面。

paras.en: The analysis turned up a wealth of findings.
paras.zh: 分析得出了大量结论。

paras.en: There was evidence of DNA from multiple human lineages, including from Europe and the Middle East, as well as genetic material from animals including dogs, cats, pigs, horses, cattle, and chickens.
paras.zh: 有证据表明DNA来自多个人类谱系，包括来自欧洲和中东的DNA，以及来自狗、猫、猪、马、牛和鸡等动物的遗传物质。

paras.en: There were also indications that the Shroud has come into contact with Mediterranean red coral, used extensively in the past for jewelry and decoration, as well as fragments of crops such as wheat and maize.
paras.zh: 还有迹象表明，裹尸布接触到了过去广泛用于珠宝和装饰的地中海红珊瑚，以及小麦和玉米等农作物的碎片。

paras.en: Elements of carrots, bananas, oranges, peanuts, and potatoes were also found.
paras.zh: 还发现了胡萝卜、香蕉、橙子、花生和土豆的成分。

paras.en: Maize and peanuts are American crops, and bananas and oranges arrived in Europe along trade routes that opened late.
paras.zh: 玉米和花生是美国农作物，香蕉和橙子则沿着开通较晚的贸易路线抵达欧洲。

paras.en: Taken together, Barcaccia and colleagues argue, the plant and animal traces point to contamination no earlier than the Late Middle Ages, in the centuries after Marco Polo and Columbus.
paras.zh: 巴卡恰及其同事认为，总而言之，植物和动物痕迹表明污染不早于中世纪晚期，即马可波罗和哥伦布之后的几个世纪。

paras.en: "While the DNA evidence cannot answer all the questions about the age or authenticity of the cloth, it provides novel insights into its biological history and demonstrates how advances in forensic science can unlock new information from historical artifacts," says Procopio.
paras.zh: 普罗科皮奥说：“虽然 DNA 证据无法回答有关布料的年龄或真实性的所有问题，但它提供了对其生物学历史的新颖见解，并展示了法医学的进步如何从历史文物中解锁新信息。”

paras.en: Much of the human DNA that the team spotted matched the late Professor Pierluigi Baima Bollone. He's the researcher who back in 1978 collected the samples from the Shroud of Turin that this latest study reanalyzes.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现的大部分人类 DNA 与已故的皮耶路易吉·拜马·博洛内 (Pierluigi Baima Bollone) 教授相匹配。他是一名研究人员，早在 1978 年就从都灵裹尸布收集了样本，这项最新研究对这些样本进行了重新分析。

paras.en: Outside of the DNA work, radiocarbon analysis of two threads collected from the Shroud's reliquary dated them to 1451–1622 CE and 1642–1800 CE, much later than the Shroud itself.
paras.zh: 在 DNA 工作之外，对从裹尸布圣物箱中收集的两条线进行放射性碳分析，将其追溯到公元 1451-1622 年和公元 1642-1800 年，比裹尸布本身晚得多。

paras.en: Those dates overlap with periods when the cloth is known to have been repaired: in 1534, after a fire at Chambéry, and again in 1694.
paras.zh: 这些日期与已知的布料修复时间重叠：1534 年，尚贝里火灾后，以及 1694 年。

paras.en: "Our findings constitute a novel and significant contribution to the field, thoroughly elucidating the biological traces left by centuries of social, cultural, and ecological engagement," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“我们的研究结果对该领域做出了新颖且重大的贡献，彻底阐明了几个世纪的社会、文化和生态参与留下的生物痕迹。”

paras.en: There are still a lot of questions remaining about the origin and authenticity of the Shroud of Turin, but this latest analysis adds plenty of background context – and shows that as scientific techniques improve, we can learn much more about this famous piece of cloth.
paras.zh: 关于都灵裹尸布的起源和真实性仍然存在很多问题，但最新的分析增加了大量的背景知识，并表明随着科学技术的进步，我们可以更多地了解这块著名的裹尸布。

paras.en: Further insights might be gathered by comparing the findings here with other ancient textiles and artifacts, according to the researchers, and these advanced methods have again proved how effective they are at identifying DNA signatures.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，通过将这里的发现与其他古代纺织品和文物进行比较，可以收集更多的见解，而这些先进的方法再次证明了它们在识别 DNA 特征方面的有效性。

paras.en: "The Shroud of Turin continues to fascinate historians, scientists, and the public," says Procopio.
paras.zh: “都灵裹尸布继续让历史学家、科学家和公众着迷，”普罗科皮奥说。

paras.en: "We're thrilled to reveal new information about the biological complexity preserved within samples collected almost 50 years ago by applying new cutting-edge forensic DNA technologies."
paras.zh: “我们很高兴能够通过应用新的尖端法医 DNA 技术揭示近 50 年前收集的样本中保存的生物复杂性的新信息。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Scientific Reports.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学报告》上。

articles.title: Blood Vessel Function Improves Within 1 Hour of Taking This Anti-Aging Supplement, Study Shows
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: One of the reasons that our health becomes more precarious as we age is that our blood vessels stiffen up and become less flexible, which can increase the risk of higher blood pressure and cardiovascular issues.
paras.zh: 随着年龄的增长，我们的健康变得更加不稳定的原因之一是我们的血管变硬且变得不那么灵活，这会增加患高血压和心血管问题的风险。

paras.en: Now researchers led by a team from the University of Surrey in the UK may have discovered a new way to counteract that gradual decline in blood vessel flexibility.
paras.zh: 现在，由英国萨里大学的一个团队领导的研究人员可能已经发现了一种抵消血管灵活性逐渐下降的新方法。

paras.en: They tested an already-available longevity and anti-aging supplement called Novos Core in 61 people aged over 40.
paras.zh: 他们在 61 名 40 岁以上的人身上测试了一种名为 Novos Core 的现有长寿和抗衰老补充剂。

paras.en: A little over half of the participants got Novos Core in a powdered formula, while the others were given a placebo powder.
paras.zh: 略多于一半的参与者服用了配方奶粉中的 Novos Core，而其他参与者则服用了安慰剂粉末。

paras.en: Both groups were followed for six months, while researchers kept tabs on the participants' cardiovascular health, including the work done by the lining of the blood vessels (the endothelium).
paras.zh: 两组患者都被跟踪了六个月，同时研究人员密切关注参与者的心血管健康状况，包括血管内皮（内皮）所做的工作。

paras.en: The final results showed a positive association between Novos Core and blood vessel function: not only did blood vessels start to behave in a more youthful way, some of the improvements were seen after just an hour.
paras.zh: 最终结果显示 Novos Core 与血管功能之间存在正相关关系：血管不仅开始表现得更年轻，而且仅仅一个小时后就看到了一些改善。

paras.en: "In apparently healthy adults, six months of daily intake of a multi-ingredient nutritional powder formulation was associated with favorable changes in vascular aging markers, including improved endothelial function, reduced device-derived arterial stiffness, and lower systolic blood pressure compared with control," write the researchers in their published paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在发表的论文中写道：“在表面上健康的成年人中，每天摄入多成分营养粉配方的六个月与血管老化标志物的有利变化相关，包括改善内皮功能、减少设备源性动脉僵硬度以及与对照组相比降低收缩压。”

paras.en: For those in the Novos Core group, blood vessels got better at widening to allow more blood through, while arteries became softer and less stiff.
paras.zh: 对于 Novos Core 组的人来说，血管能够更好地扩张，以允许更多的血液通过，同时动脉变得更柔软、不那么僵硬。

paras.en: Blood pressure in these participants went down too – systolic blood pressure (the top number in readings) dropped by 6.1 mmHg more on average than for those in the placebo group.
paras.zh: 这些参与者的血压也下降了——收缩压（读数中最高的数字）比安慰剂组平均下降了 6.1 毫米汞柱。

paras.en: The 10-year estimated risk of heart attacks and strokes went down for the Novos Core group too, but it's important to bear in mind these events weren't tracked. There was no difference in low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol reduction between the two groups – the 'bad' cholesterol linked with poorer heart health.
paras.zh: Novos Core 组的 10 年心脏病发作和中风估计风险也有所下降，但重要的是要记住这些事件没有被跟踪。两组之间的低密度脂蛋白（LDL）胆固醇降低没有差异——“坏”胆固醇与较差的心脏健康有关。

paras.en: As an anti-aging supplement, Novos Core combines several ingredients that researchers have previously linked to slower biological aging, including magnesium, glucosamine, ginger extract, and vitamin C.
paras.zh: 作为一种抗衰老补充剂，Novos Core 结合了研究人​​员之前认为可以减缓生物衰老的多种成分，包括镁、葡萄糖胺、生姜提取物和维生素 C。

paras.en: "The formulation evaluated in the present study was selected to combine ingredients with prior evidence of relevance to complementary biological domains implicated in aging and vascular dysfunction, including endothelial function, redox balance, inflammatory signaling, metabolic regulation, and vascular tone," write the researchers.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“本研究中评估的配方被选择将成分与先前证据相结合，这些证据与衰老和血管功能障碍相关的互补生物领域相关，包括内皮功能、氧化还原平衡、炎症信号、代谢调节和血管张力。”

paras.en: Now we know that some of those ingredients are apparently acting on blood vessel function, which may explain why they're already associated with the body's aging process and better cardiovascular health.
paras.zh: 现在我们知道其中一些成分显然对血管功能起作用，这可以解释为什么它们已经与身体的衰老过程和更好的心血管健康相关。

paras.en: There's still plenty of research work left to be done, though. The blood health markers that the study looked at are significant, but the participants weren't followed to see who did or didn't go on to have heart health problems in the future.
paras.zh: 不过，仍有大量研究工作有待完成。该研究考察的血液健康指标很重要，但没有对参与者进行跟踪，看看谁在未来会出现或不会出现心脏健康问题。

paras.en: "The findings provide an interesting proof of concept, but the important next step is to understand the underlying biology and establish whether changes in cardiovascular biomarkers translate into meaningful longer-term health benefits," says Juliet Wright, the Founding Dean of Medicine at the University of Surrey, who wasn't directly involved in the research.
paras.zh: “这些发现提供了一个有趣的概念证明，但重要的下一步是了解潜在的生物学，并确定心血管生物标志物的变化是否转化为有意义的长期健康益处，”萨里大学医学院创始院长朱丽叶·赖特（Juliet Wright）说，她没有直接参与这项研究。

paras.en: Further research would be able to look at larger, more diverse groups of people, and perhaps tease out the effects of the different ingredients in Novos Core. Right now, it's tricky to know which of its various compounds are having the most effect.
paras.zh: 进一步的研究将能够观察更大、更多样化的人群，或许还能弄清楚 Novos Core 中不同成分的影响。目前，很难知道其中哪种化合物最有效。

paras.en: It's also worth noting that the funding for the research came from the Novos company that makes Novos Core, though the paper declares that Novos "had no role" in the study design, or the "collection, primary analysis or interpretation of data".
paras.zh: 还值得注意的是，该研究的资金来自生产 Novos Core 的 Novos 公司，尽管该论文声称 Novos 在研究设计或“数据的收集、初步分析或解释”中“没有任何作用”。

paras.en: Related: A Cheap Daily Supplement Seems to Boost Brain Function in Older Adults
paras.zh: 相关：廉价的每日补充剂似乎可以增强老年人的大脑功能

paras.en: "These findings are encouraging," says Christian Heiss, a professor of cardiovascular medicine at the University of Surrey.
paras.zh: “这些发现令人鼓舞，”萨里大学心血管医学教授克里斯蒂安·海斯说。

paras.en: "We now need larger studies to understand the mechanisms involved and, importantly, whether these changes translate into longer-term health benefits."
paras.zh: “我们现在需要更大规模的研究来了解所涉及的机制，更重要的是，了解这些变化是否会转化为长期的健康益处。”

paras.en: The research has been published in European Heart Journal Open.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《欧洲心脏杂志开放》上。

articles.title: A Cheap Daily Supplement Seems to Boost Brain Function in Older Adults
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: Cheap daily supplements are changing how scientists view the gut and its connection to the brain.
paras.zh: 廉价的日常补充剂正在改变科学家对肠道及其与大脑的联系的看法。

paras.en: In 2024, a rigorous twin study published in Nature Communications found that taking daily protein and prebiotic supplements can improve memory test scores in people over age 60.
paras.zh: 2024 年，《自然通讯》发表的一项严格的双胞胎研究发现，每日服用蛋白质和益生元补充剂可以提高 60 岁以上人群的记忆力测试成绩。

paras.en: The study has been cited more than 100 times since, and the idea has inspired whole new clinical trials investigating how some supplements may protect against dementia.
paras.zh: 自那以后，这项研究已被引用超过 100 次，这个想法激发了全新的临床试验，研究某些补充剂如何预防痴呆症。

paras.en: Later that year, scientists at Wageningen University in the Netherlands launched the PRECODE clinical trial, which stands for Gut-brain Health Effects of PREbiotics in Older Adults With Suspected COgnitive DEcline.
paras.zh: 同年晚些时候，荷兰瓦赫宁根大学的科学家启动了 PRECODE 临床试验，该试验代表益生元对疑似认知能力下降的老年人的肠脑健康影响。

paras.en: It's the first human study to investigate the combined cognitive and microbial effects of three distinct dietary fibers: chicory inulin, resistant dextrin, and seaweed polysaccharide, compared to a placebo (maltodextrin).
paras.zh: 这是第一项人体研究，调查三种不同膳食纤维（菊苣菊粉、抗性糊精和海藻多糖）与安慰剂（麦芽糖糊精）相比对认知和微生物的综合影响。

paras.en: For 26 weeks, participants over 60 have consumed these dietary fibers twice a day, mixed into water, tea, or coffee, and they have had regular brain scans and cognitive tests to track how they are faring.
paras.zh: 在 26 周的时间里，60 岁以上的参与者每天两次食用这些膳食纤维，将其混合到水、茶或咖啡中，并且他们定期进行脑部扫描和认知测试，以跟踪他们的情况。

paras.en: We'll know more in 2027 when the trial finishes.
paras.zh: 2027 年审判结束后我们将会了解更多信息。

paras.en: Inulin, a dietary fiber in the fructan class, is the same dietary supplement that proved so good for the brain in that first 2024 twin study.
paras.zh: 菊粉是一种果聚糖类膳食纤维，在 2024 年的第一项双胞胎研究中证明它对大脑非常有益。

paras.en: Watch the video below for a summary of the 2024 study:
paras.zh: 观看下面的视频，了解 2024 年研究的摘要：

paras.en: During that double-blind trial, researchers tested two inexpensive plant-fiber prebiotics that are available over the counter in many countries.
paras.zh: 在那次双盲试验中，研究人员测试了两种廉价的植物纤维益生元，这些益生元在许多国家都可以在柜台购买。

paras.en: The other, fructooligosaccharide (FOS), is a plant carbohydrate often used as a natural low-calorie sweetener.
paras.zh: 另一种是低聚果糖（FOS），是一种植物碳水化合物，通常用作天然低热量甜味剂。

paras.en: To look into how these supplements affected the aging brain, researchers at King's College London enrolled 36 pairs of twins, all at least 60 years old.
paras.zh: 为了研究这些补充剂如何影响衰老的大脑，伦敦国王学院的研究人员招募了 36 对双胞胎，他们的年龄都至少 60 岁。

paras.en: Each duo was randomly split: one twin received a daily prebiotic mixed into protein powder, while the other received a placebo powder.
paras.zh: 每对双胞胎被随机分成：双胞胎中的一个每天服用混合在蛋白粉中的益生元，而另一个则服用安慰剂粉。

paras.en: The twins who unknowingly took inulin or FOS generally scored higher on a cognitive test three months later.
paras.zh: 在不知情的情况下服用菊粉或低聚果糖的双胞胎在三个月后的认知测试中通常得分更高。

paras.en: What's more, the daily fiber supplements were linked to subtle changes in the gut microbiome between twins.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，每日纤维补充剂与双胞胎肠道微生物群的微妙变化有关。

paras.en: The beneficial Bifidobacterium, for instance, was more plentiful in those taking inulin or FOS.
paras.zh: 例如，服用菊粉或低聚果糖的人体内有益的​​双歧杆菌含量更高。

paras.en: Studies on mice suggest that Bifidobacterium reduces cognitive deficits by regulating gut-brain connections.
paras.zh: 对小鼠的研究表明，双歧杆菌通过调节肠脑连接来减少认知缺陷。

paras.en: "We are excited to see these changes in just 12 weeks. This holds huge promise for enhancing brain health and memory in our aging population," said Mary Ni Lochlainn, a geriatric medicine researcher at King's College London, when the findings were published in 2024.
paras.zh: “我们很高兴在短短 12 周内看到这些变化。这对于增强老年人的大脑健康和记忆力有着巨大的希望，”伦敦国王学院老年医学研究员 Mary Ni Lochlainn 在 2024 年发表研究结果时说道。

paras.en: "Unlocking the secrets of the gut-brain axis could offer new approaches for living more healthily for longer."
paras.zh: “解开肠脑轴的秘密可以为更健康、更长久地生活提供新方法。”

paras.en: King's College London (KCL) is home to the UK's largest adult twin registry, and twin studies are highly valuable when it comes to differentiating between the effects of genetics and the environment on human health.
paras.zh: 伦敦国王学院 (KCL) 是英国最大的成人双胞胎登记处，双胞胎研究对于区分遗传和环境对人类健康的影响非常有价值。

paras.en: Past studies on rodents suggest that high-fiber supplements, such as inulin and FOS, can 'feed' the colon's microbiome, allowing 'good' bacteria to thrive.
paras.zh: 过去对啮齿动物的研究表明，高纤维补充剂，如菊粉和低聚果糖，可以“喂养”结肠的微生物群，让“好”细菌茁壮成长。

paras.en: Some of these bacterial players are also linked to improved cognitive function in both mice and humans.
paras.zh: 其中一些细菌也与小鼠和人类认知功能的改善有关。

paras.en: Some experts are now so convinced by the results that they refer to the gut as the body's 'second brain'.
paras.zh: 现在，一些专家对这些结果深信不疑，他们将肠道称为人体的“第二大脑”。

paras.en: But the way these two nervous systems work together remains a mystery.
paras.zh: 但这两个神经系统如何协同工作仍然是个谜。

paras.en: The twin study at KCL hints that consuming certain 'brain foods' could be a promising way to treat cognitive decline, adding to research suggesting key nutrients may be able to slow its progress.
paras.zh: 伦敦皇家学院的双胞胎研究暗示，食用某些“健脑食品”可能是治疗认知能力下降的一种有前途的方法，并补充了表明关键营养素可能能够减缓其进展的研究。

paras.en: "These plant fibers, which are cheap and available over the counter, could benefit a wide group of people in these cash-strapped times. They are safe and acceptable too," said geriatrician Claire Steves at KCL.
paras.zh: “这些植物纤维价格便宜，可以在柜台上买到，在这个现金短缺的时代可以让很多人受益。它们也安全且可以接受，”伦敦国王学院的老年病学家克莱尔·史蒂夫斯说。

paras.en: "Our next task is to see whether these effects are sustained over longer periods and in larger groups of people."
paras.zh: “我们的下一个任务是看看这些影响是否会在更长的时间内、在更大的人群中持续存在。”

paras.en: That's what the PRECODE trial seeks to address.
paras.zh: 这就是 PRECODE 试验试图解决的问题。

paras.en: The trial investigators hope this ongoing study into fiber supplements will "provide an in-depth evaluation of the microbiota-gut-brain axis in older adults, at risk of cognitive decline."
paras.zh: 试验研究人员希望这项正在进行的纤维补充剂研究能够“对面临认知能力下降风险的老年人的微生物群-肠-脑轴进行深入评估”。

paras.en: Related: One Common Vitamin May Lower Toxic Alzheimer's Proteins, Research Suggests
paras.zh: 相关：研究表明，一种常见的维生素可以降低有毒的阿尔茨海默氏症蛋白质

paras.en: In 2025, researchers reported that in humans and mice, a lower Bifidobacterium-to-Akkermansia ratio in the gut microbiome is linked to multiple sclerosis, and this imbalance was also associated with more severe disease.
paras.zh: 2025 年，研究人员报告称，在人类和小鼠中，肠道微生物组中双歧杆菌与阿克曼氏菌的比率较低与多发性硬化症有关，而这种不平衡也与更严重的疾病有关。

paras.en: Whether these deficiencies can be remedied with supplements, however, remains unknown.
paras.zh: 然而，这些缺陷是否可以通过补充剂来弥补仍然未知。

paras.en: The gut has its fingers in many bodily 'pies', including the immune system and the central nervous system.
paras.zh: 肠道参与了许多身体“馅饼”，包括免疫系统和中枢神经系统。

paras.en: Feeding its microbiome certain prebiotics and probiotics could open the door to treating a plethora of illnesses and diseases.
paras.zh: 向其微生物组喂食某些益生元和益生菌可以为治疗多种疾病打开大门。

paras.en: The PRECODE trial could give us a first taste of that possibility.
paras.zh: PRECODE 试验可以让我们第一次尝到这种可能性。

paras.en: The twin study was published in Nature Communications.
paras.zh: 这项双胞胎研究发表在《自然通讯》上。

articles.title: Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation

paras.en: Two monster black holes from the dawn of time defy explanation
paras.zh: 两个来自创世之初的怪物黑洞无法解释

paras.en: Association of Universities for Research in Astronomy (AURA)
paras.zh: 天文学研究大学协会 (AURA)

paras.en: Astronomers have discovered the oldest known compact pair of quasars, powered by two enormous black holes that existed just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Weighing an astonishing 1.5 billion and 400 million times the mass of the Sun, these cosmic giants somehow grew to incredible sizes far earlier than current theories can explain.
paras.zh: 天文学家发现了已知最古老的致密类星体对，它们由大爆炸后仅 9 亿年就存在的两个巨大黑洞提供动力。这些宇宙巨星的质量惊人，分别是太阳质量的 15 亿倍和 4 亿倍，它们以某种方式增长到令人难以置信的尺寸，远远早于当前理论所能解释的时间。

paras.en: Astronomers have identified an extraordinary pair of quasars dating back to just 900 million years after the Big Bang. Each is powered by an enormous black hole that somehow grew to an astonishing size when the Universe was still in its infancy. Scientists have no definitive explanation for how these two cosmic giants became so massive so quickly. The remarkable pair has been given the Hawaiian name Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua.
paras.zh: 天文学家发现了一对非凡的类星体，其历史可以追溯到大爆炸后仅 9 亿年。每一个都由一个巨大的黑洞提供动力，当宇宙还处于婴儿期时，这个黑洞不知何故就增长到了惊人的大小。对于这两个宇宙巨星为何如此迅速地变得如此巨大，科学家们还没有明确的解释。这对非凡的情侣被赋予了夏威夷语名字 Nāpōwawa'enakaulua。

paras.en: An international research team has discovered the most distant compact pair of quasars ever observed, offering a rare glimpse into the earliest stages of cosmic history. Officially designated J1602+4228AB and nicknamed Nāpōwawāʻenakaulua, the pair also holds the record for the closest separation between two known quasars from the early period known as cosmic dawn.
paras.zh: 一个国际研究小组发现了迄今为止观测到的最遥远的致密类星体对，为了解宇宙历史的最早阶段提供了难得的机会。官方命名为 J1602+4228AB，绰号为 Nāpōwawā´enakaulua，这对星体还保持着早期宇宙黎明时期两个已知类星体之间最接近距离的记录。

paras.en: Although astronomers believe paired quasars should be relatively common, finding and studying them is exceptionally difficult. Discovering two so close together, especially from such an early period in the Universe's history, makes this finding particularly remarkable.
paras.zh: 尽管天文学家认为成对类星体应该相对常见，但发现和研究它们却异常困难。发现两个距离如此之近，尤其是在宇宙历史的如此早期阶段，使这一发现显得尤为引人注目。

paras.en: The discovery was made possible by combining observations from the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) and the Gemini North telescope on Maunakea, a dormant volcano in Hawai'i. The research was led by Silvia Onorato, a postdoctoral research associate at NSF NOIRLab, and is described in a paper published in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.
paras.zh: 这一发现是通过詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜（JWST）和夏威夷莫纳克亚休眠火山上的双子座北望远镜的观测相结合而实现的。这项研究由 NSF NOIRLab 博士后研究员 Silvia Onorato 领导，并在《天体物理学杂志快报》上发表的一篇论文中进行了描述。

paras.en: Gemini North is one of the two telescopes that make up the International Gemini Observatory. Operated by NSF NOIRLab, the observatory is an international partnership led by the U.S. National Science Foundation, with participation from Canada, Chile, Brazil, Argentina, and the Republic of Korea.
paras.zh: 双子座北站是组成国际双子座天文台的两座望远镜之一。该天文台由 NSF NOIRLab 运营，是一个由美国国家科学基金会领导、加拿大、智利、巴西、阿根廷和韩国参与的国际合作项目。

paras.en: How Giant Black Holes Formed in the Early Universe
paras.zh: 早期宇宙中巨大的黑洞是如何形成的

paras.en: During the first billion years after the Big Bang, the Universe underwent a period of extraordinary transformation.
